title: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
capsule: Proclaimed a federal socialist republic on 29 November 1945 (formally renamed in 1963), Tito's Yugoslavia united six constituent republics under one-party communist rule while pursuing an independent path after the 1948 Tito-Stalin split and co-founding the Non-Aligned Movement in 1961. A relatively liberal 'market socialism' and open borders distinguished it from the Soviet bloc, but after Tito's death in 1980 mounting nationalist tensions and economic crisis eroded federal authority, and the federation disintegrated in 1991-1992 as Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Macedonia seceded, leaving only Serbia and Montenegro in a rump state.
